survivors.name: Market intraday momentum, first-half-hour signal η(r1) — Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018), JFE 129(2), 394–414
survivors.instrument: SPY (S&P 500 ETF), TAQ data. Footnote 2 verbatim: 'The results are similar when we use the S&P 500 futures, another tradable asset on the index (see the internet appendix)' — the futures result is asserted, not shown in the paper.
survivors.timeframe: 13 half-hour buckets per RTH day. Signal from bucket 1 (previous close → 10:00 ET). Trade held in bucket 13 (15:30–16:00 ET).
survivors.rules:
VERIFIED MECHANICAL. Session 09:30–16:00 ET, split into 13 half-hour buckets, r_j,t = p_j,t / p_(j-1),t - 1.

CRITICAL DEFINITION (verified verbatim): p_0,t = p_13,t-1, the PREVIOUS trading day's 16:00 price. So r1 is measured from the previous close to 10:00 and deliberately spans the overnight gap. The paper states this is 'so that the first half-hour return captures the impact of information released after the previous day's market close'.
  r1_t  = p(10:00,t) / p(16:00,t-1) - 1
  r12_t = p(15:30,t) / p(15:00,t) - 1
  r13_t = p(16:00,t) / p(15:30,t) - 1

ENTRY (primary rule η(r1)): at 15:30:00 ET on day t — r1_t has been known since 10:00, so no look-ahead:
  if r1_t > 0  -> long
  if r1_t <= 0 -> short
No flat state; exactly zero maps to SHORT (Eq. 4 verified).

STOP LOSS: none.

EXIT: unconditionally at the 16:00 ET close, in the closing auction. Verbatim: 'the position (long or short) is closed at the market close on each trading day.'

SIZE: 100% of capital, unlevered.

DAY FILTER: exclude any trading day with fewer than 100 trades in SPY.

COST MODEL to reproduce the paper's net figures: pay the half-spread on the 15:30 ENTRY ONLY — buy at the 15:30 ask if long, sell at the 15:30 bid if short. Pay NO spread on the exit, because (verbatim) 'the closing of the SPY is uniquely traded at the market clearing price for all the buys and sells, there will be no bid/ask spread effect for the price at 4:00pm.' Commissions are excluded by assumption (footnote 14). If you port this to ES/NQ futures there is no single closing cross, so you must pay the spread on BOTH legs — the paper's net numbers do not transfer.

VARIANT η(r12): same, signal = r12_t.
VARIANT η(r1,r12): long only if r1_t > 0 AND r12_t > 0; short only if r1_t <= 0 AND r12_t <= 0; otherwise NO POSITION that day.
survivors.evidence: VERIFIED against full text. Sample 1 Feb 1993 – 31 Dec 2013. Predictive regression r13 = α + β·r1: slope ×100 = 6.94, significant at 1%, in-sample R² 1.6%; r12 alone R² 1.1%; both 2.6%. Expanding-window OOS R²: 1.4% (r1), 0.9% (r12), 2.0% (both). Strategy results annualized BEFORE costs, confirmed in text: η(r1) 6.67% return, Sharpe 1.08, skew 0.90, success 54.37%; η(r12) 1.77%, Sharpe 0.29, success 50.93%; η(r1,r12) 4.39%, success 77.05%. Benchmarks: Always Long -1.11%, Sharpe -0.18, success 50.42%; Buy-and-Hold 6.04%, 20.57% s.d., Sharpe 0.29. TRANSACTION COSTS: modelled from actual TAQ bid/ask at 15:30, entry leg only, commissions ignored. Post-decimalization (after 1 Jul 2001): η(r1) falls from 6.93% to 4.46% p.a. net, s.d. 6.10%; η(r1,r12) reduced by only 1.22% to 4.30% net. Post 1 Jan 2005 (spread stabilized ~1.2 bp): η(r1) 6.52% net vs 7.96% gross.
survivors.why_credible: SSRN returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch; I verified against the full working-paper text (Gao, Iowa State; Han, UNC Charlotte; Li, Rutgers; Zhou, WashU) and every claimed figure matched. Published JFE 129(2), 394–414. The foundational peer-reviewed paper for this whole literature, ~20 years of data, genuine expanding-window OOS R², and it shows gross and net side by side. Two caveats that matter for a futures bot: (1) it is SPY, not ES/NQ — the futures result is relegated to an unpublished internet appendix; (2) Baltussen et al. (candidate 1), on a longer sample and on actual futures, found this exact first-half-hour signal has a NEGATIVE OOS R² of -1.68% on ES. If you build one of these, build the rROD version, not this one.

survivors.name: Noise Area intraday momentum ('Beat the Market') — Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon (2024), SSRN 4824172 / Swiss Finance Institute 24-97
survivors.instrument: SPY (S&P 500 ETF), IQFeed data. Robustness on 33 global futures: 21 commodities + 12 equity indices — and contrary to the brief, the four US equity index futures ARE named, including Nasdaq and S&P500.
survivors.timeframe: Intraday. Decisions evaluated ONLY on the half-hour grid (HH:00 and HH:30) between 09:30 and 16:00 ET. Flat overnight.
survivors.rules:
MECHANICAL, BUT THE PAPER ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT — two rules must come from the authors' reference code. See the last paragraph.

1) GRID: entries, stops and reversals are evaluated only at HH:00 and HH:30 stamps between 09:30 and 16:00 ET. Verbatim: 'trading is restricted to semi-hourly intervals, specifically at HH:00 and HH:30' and 'Stop losses can also be triggered only on semi-hourly intervals.' A mid-bar excursion is ignored.

2) SIGMA: for each grid stamp HH:MM,
   move_{t-i,HH:MM} = |Close_{t-i,HH:MM} / Open_{t-i,09:30} - 1|, for i = 1..14
   sigma_{t,HH:MM} = (1/14) * sum of those 14 values

3) BOUNDARIES (gap-adjusted, verified verbatim):
   UpperBound_{t,HH:MM} = max(Open_{t,09:30}, Close_{t-1,16:00}) * (1 + sigma_{t,HH:MM})
   LowerBound_{t,HH:MM} = min(Open_{t,09:30}, Close_{t-1,16:00}) * (1 - sigma_{t,HH:MM})
   The band widens through the day because sigma grows with elapsed time.

4) ENTRY (when flat), at a grid stamp only: price > UpperBound -> LONG; price < LowerBound -> SHORT; inside the band -> stay flat.

5) EXIT / TRAILING STOP (best variant), checked at each subsequent grid stamp:
   Long  TrailingStop_{t,HH:MM} = max(UpperBound_{t,HH:MM}, VWAP_{t,HH:MM})
   Short TrailingStop_{t,HH:MM} = min(LowerBound_{t,HH:MM}, VWAP_{t,HH:MM})
   Close the position the moment price crosses it (evaluated on the grid). VWAP is computed from RTH data only and resets daily. A cross of the OPPOSITE boundary closes the position AND opens a new one in the opposite direction in the same action.

6) HARD EXIT: all positions closed at 16:00 ET. Nothing is held overnight.

7) SIZING (headline variant), verified verbatim:
   Shares_t = floor( AUM_{t-1} * min(4, 0.02 / sigma_SPY,t) / Open_{t,09:30} )
   where sigma_SPY,t is the SAMPLE standard deviation of the previous 14 daily returns using the 1/13 divisor (Bessel-corrected), target vol = 2% daily, leverage hard-capped at 4x.

8) COSTS: $0.0035/share commission (IB entry-level tiered) + $0.001/share slippage, applied on both legs.

TWO RULES NOT IN THE PAPER. I verified the published text specifies neither of these, yet an independent replication reports both are required to reproduce the 1,985% / SR 1.33 headline: (a) VWAP must be computed on TYPICAL PRICE (High+Low+Close)/3, not on close; (b) there is a VWAP CONFIRMATION at entry — a long additionally requires price > VWAP, a short additionally requires price < VWAP, on top of the boundary break. Without these you will not reproduce the paper. The paper is therefore not self-sufficient; you must implement against the authors' published Python reference code, not the PDF.

(c) same plus vol-targeted sizing — 1,985% total, 19.6% IRR, 14.3% vol, Sharpe 1.33, MDD 25%, hit ~43%, alpha 19.6%, best trade +9.1%, worst trade -2.9%. SPY buy-and-hold same window: 227%, 7.2% IRR, 20.2% vol, Sharpe 0.45. Kissell I-Star stress test confirmed verbatim: Large Cap parameters a1=687, a2=0.70, a3=0.72; Sharpe falls 1.33 -> 1.17, yearly alpha stays above 15%. FUTURES ROBUSTNESS (FAQ Q13), Jan 2007 – Sep 2024, 33 futures: only 2 of 33 negative, AVERAGE per-instrument Sharpe 0.60, all-asset diversified portfolio Sharpe 1.65. CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF: the futures table is only PARTLY redacted — the four US equity index futures are named. Nasdaq: 1,533% total, 16.8% CAGR, 13.6% vol, SR 1.23, MDD 26%, hit 43%, skew 2.1. survivors.why_credible: SSRN abstract_id 4824172 VERIFIED as correct (also Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper N°24-97, published 10 May 2024, authors Zarattini/Aziz/Barbon — Barbon is University of St. Gallen). SSRN blocks automated fetch; verified against the full Concretum PDF text and every figure matched. NOT peer-reviewed. Its real strength is being the most honestly costed study here — commissions plus live-calibrated slippage, then stress-tested with a published market-impact model. Four things to weigh against it: (1) the headline 19.6%/1.33 depends on 4x leverage and vol-targeting bolted onto a base whose unlevered Sharpe is 0.61; (2) the three variants are presented in improving order, the signature of in-sample refinement, with no held-out period; (3) a 43% hit ratio means the entire edge lives in tail asymmetry — one badly-handled gap kills it; (4) the paper is not reproducible from its own text, per the two missing VWAP rules above. Separately, a replication document present in this project's fetched-source cache (Delgado, dated Aug 2026) reproduces 1,989%/SR 1.317 on the paper window but reports the 2 Sep 2025 – 14 Aug 2026 stretch returning -8.1% at Sharpe -0.461 — I could NOT verify that document's source URL via arXiv or web search, so treat it as unconfirmed, but it is a reason to forward-test before sizing. Direct PDF: https://concretumgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Beat-the-Market.pdf

survivors.name: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (JFE 2018) — first-half-hour → last-half-hour timing [MECHANICAL, VERIFIED]
survivors.instrument: SPY. Robustness on 10 further ETFs (QQQ, IWM, DIA, EEM, FXI, EFA, VWO, XLF, IYR, TLT). Futures results are claimed in footnote 2 but live only in an unretrievable internet appendix — treat 'works on ES' as UNVERIFIED from this source.
survivors.timeframe: 13 half-hour buckets/day, US/Eastern. Signal window: previous 16:00 close → 10:00. Traded window: 15:30 → 16:00.
survivors.rules:
FULLY MECHANICAL — no discretion. DATA: SPY trade prices, tz=America/New_York, regular session.
PRICE POINTS on day t:
  P0  = official closing price of day t-1 (16:00:00 auction print)
  P1  = last trade at or before 10:00:00 on day t
  P11 = last trade at or before 15:00:00 on day t
  P12 = last trade at or before 15:30:00 on day t
  P13 = official closing price of day t (16:00:00 auction print)
SIGNALS (fully known by 15:30:00, computed on closed data only):
  r1  = P1/P0  - 1   (spans the overnight gap PLUS the first 30 min; p_0,t = p_13,t-1)
  r12 = P12/P11 - 1  (the 15:00→15:30 bar)
DAY FILTER: skip day t entirely if SPY printed fewer than 500 trades that day (paper's own filter, verified p.4).
VARIANT A (headline, eq. 4): ENTRY at exactly 15:30:00, one market order, 100% of equity, no leverage: r1 > 0 → LONG; r1 <= 0 → SHORT. A signal of exactly zero goes SHORT (the paper's inequality is strict on the long side only).
VARIANT B (two-signal, eq. 5): ENTRY at 15:30:00: LONG iff (r1 > 0 AND r12 > 0); SHORT iff (r1 <= 0 AND r12 <= 0); OTHERWISE NO TRADE — stay flat the whole day.
STOP: NONE. Verified: the paper specifies no stop, no target and no intraday management. The position is unprotected for the full 30 minutes; worst case is the entire 15:30→16:00 move. Any stop you add is your own parameter and invalidates the quoted statistics.
EXIT: market-on-close order, filled at the 16:00:00 closing auction price. Always flat overnight. Exactly one entry and at most one exit per day. Verbatim: "the position (long or short) is closed at the market close on each trading day".
COST MODEL AS BACKTESTED (to reproduce Table 10): pay the 15:30 ask to open a long, receive the 15:30 bid to open a short; close at the 16:00 auction with ZERO spread ("there will be no bid/ask spread effect for the price at 4:00pm"); commissions EXCLUDED (footnote 14, verified verbatim).
RETURN CONVENTION: the strategy return is the raw 30-minute return, annualised by multiplying by 252 (footnote 10).

survivors.name: Noise Area intraday momentum on ES/NQ futures (Quantitativo adaptation of Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon)
survivors.instrument: E-mini S&P 500 (ES) and E-mini Nasdaq-100 (NQ) futures, front month. Micro equivalents (MES multiplier $5, MNQ multiplier $2) trade identically. Quantitativo also reports a 3-sleeve portfolio: 50% NQ strategy / 25% ES strategy / 25% NQ passive long.
survivors.timeframe: 1-minute bars for computation, HH:00/HH:30 decision grid, RTH only, flat overnight
survivors.rules:
MECHANICAL SPEC (fully deterministic; steps 1-9). Symbols: t = today, i = days back, N = sigma lookback in days.

DEFAULTS I HAD TO SUPPLY (the Quantitativo article does NOT state these; I verified with a targeted re-fetch that decision frequency and session are 'not stated' there). Each is inherited verbatim from the source paper (SSRN 4824172), which the article names explicitly as its basis. They are stated here as fixed constants so the implementer exercises no discretion: (D1) decision grid = HH:00 and HH:30 only; (D2) session = RTH 09:30-16:00 ET, Globex overnight excluded from bands, VWAP and trading; (D3) VWAP price input = (H+L+C)/3 per 1-min bar; (D4) fills at next-bar open after the decision bar closes (the paper fills at the grid price itself, which is a mild look-ahead; next-bar-open is the conservative variant).

1. PARAMETERS. N = 90 days (Quantitativo 'improved' variant; N = 14 in the original paper). vol_target = 0.03 daily. leverage_cap = 8. (Original-rule variant: N = 14, vol_target = 0.02, leverage_cap = 4.)

2. DAILY ANCHORS. O_t = open of the 09:30 bar on day t. C_prev = close of the 16:00 (last RTH) bar on day t-1.

3. SIGMA (per time-of-day slot, recomputed each morning, uses only completed prior days):
   move[t-i][HH:MM] = abs( Close[t-i][HH:MM] / Open[t-i][09:30] - 1 )
   sigma[t][HH:MM]  = (1/N) * SUM over i = 1..N of move[t-i][HH:MM]
   Note: no gap adjustment inside move — it is the same-day close/open ratio. Because sigma is a ratio of same-day prices, contract rolls do not distort it; trade the front month and roll on volume crossover.

4. BANDS (gap-adjusted, recomputed for each slot):
   UB[t][HH:MM] = max(O_t, C_prev) * (1 + sigma[t][HH:MM])
   LB[t][HH:MM] = min(O_t, C_prev) * (1 - sigma[t][HH:MM])

5. VWAP. Cumulative sum((H+L+C)/3 * volume) / cumulative sum(volume), reset at 09:30, RTH volume only (the paper's footnote 2: 'VWAP is computed only using market hours data').

6. DECISION LOOP. At each grid time k in {10:00, 10:30, 11:00, ..., 15:30}, let P_k = close of the bar ending at k. Evaluate exactly once, in this order. No action at any other time.
   IF FLAT:  P_k > UB[k] -> BUY at next-bar open.  P_k < LB[k] -> SELL SHORT at next-bar open.  Otherwise nothing.
   IF LONG:  stop_k = max(UB[k], VWAP_k). IF P_k < stop_k -> exit long at next-bar open; THEN if P_k < LB[k], immediately reverse to short on the same fill; else go flat.
   IF SHORT: stop_k = min(LB[k], VWAP_k). IF P_k > stop_k -> exit short at next-bar open; THEN if P_k > UB[k], immediately reverse to long on the same fill; else go flat.
   Re-entry is allowed: a flat position that later satisfies the FLAT branch at a subsequent grid time re-enters. (In the SPY original this produces 7,668 trades / 1.8 per day over 17 years.)

7. HARD EXIT. Close any open position at the 16:00 RTH close (market-on-close), unconditionally.

8. STOPS ARE GRID-ONLY. There is no intrabar stop order. The paper is explicit: 'Stop losses can also be triggered only on semi-hourly intervals.' Do not place a resting stop; evaluate at HH:00/HH:30 and send a market order.

9. SIZING (futures adaptation of the paper's share formula):
   sigma_daily_t = sample standard deviation (divisor n-1 = 13) of the last 14 daily close-to-close returns of the underlying index.
   contracts_t = floor( AUM[t-1] * min(leverage_cap, vol_target / sigma_daily_t) / (O_t * point_multiplier) ), point_multiplier = 50 for ES, 20 for NQ.
   Size is fixed at 09:30 and held for the whole day, including after a reversal.

WARMUP: N + 1 prior RTH days for sigma, 15 for sigma_daily.

POST-COST: YES, itemised. '$0.85/contract in commissions + $1.40/contract in fees' per transaction (x2 per round turn) plus '0.25 tick in slippage in every transaction (i.e., 0.5 tick per trade)'. That works out to about $10.75 per ES round turn per contract and about $6.75 for NQ. Sample: Databento minute data, 2010 to Jan 2025 (~15 years). VERIFIED by fetching the article.

survivors.why_credible:
VERIFIED: I fetched the article and every quoted number, cost figure and parameter above matches. Costs are itemised per contract rather than hand-waved; win rate 36-38% with payoff 2.09-2.25 is internally consistent with a breakout profile; +2 bps/trade on ES is honestly small and the author does not oversell it.

CORRECTION TO THE INCOMING BRIEF: the brief flagged the 14->90 day lookback change as a 'parameter-selection red flag'. I checked this against the source paper's own sensitivity table (Q6, verified in the PDF): 'The Sharpe Ratio of the strategy remains largely unaffected by variations in the lookback period used to compute the Noise Area. Empirical evidence shows that the highest Total Returns and Sharpe Ratios are achieved with very long windows (e.g., 90 days).' Sharpe across 5/10/14/20/25/30/60/90-day lookbacks spans roughly 1.23 to 1.50, with 90 days the best. So the 90-day choice was pre-published in the source, not fitted by Quantitativo — this materially weakens the overfit objection. The 2%->3% vol target and 4x->8x cap changes remain pure leverage scaling and explain most of the CAGR jump; they are NOT alpha.

REMAINING CAVEATS: (1) no out-of-sample split at all; (2) 8x leverage is unreachable under prop-firm daily-loss rules — size this at the 4x/2% variant, which means budgeting for the ~8.1% CAGR / 0.91 Sharpe profile, not 24%; (3) the article gives no rules of its own, so this spec is really the SPY paper's engine pointed at futures — treat candidate 2 as the actual evidence base.

survivors.name: Beat the Market: intraday momentum on SPY (Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon) — the fully specified original
survivors.instrument: SPY (S&P 500 ETF). Included because it is the only version where the complete rule set, the sizing formula and the 2007-2024 sample are published in full. Substituting ES/MES is a direct swap; see candidate 1.
survivors.timeframe: 30-minute decision grid (HH:00/HH:30), RTH only, flat overnight
survivors.rules:
IDENTICAL ENGINE TO CANDIDATE 1, with these parameter values. All formulas below are transcribed verbatim from the paper PDF (version of 3 Feb 2025), not from a secondary summary.

1. SIGMA, N = 14 days. Paper's step 1: move[t-i][09:30-HH:MM] = abs( Close[t-i][HH:MM] / Open[t-i][09:30] - 1 ), i = 1..14. Step 2: sigma[t][09:30-HH:MM] = (1/14) * SUM(move[t-i][09:30-HH:MM]).

2. BANDS, verbatim: UpperBound[t][HH:MM] = max(Open[t][09:30], Close[t-1][16:00]) * (1 + sigma[t][09:30-HH:MM]); LowerBound[t][HH:MM] = min(Open[t][09:30], Close[t-1][16:00]) * (1 - sigma[t][09:30-HH:MM]). The Noise Area is the interval between them.

3. ENTRY: long if price is above the Noise Area, short if below. 'To mitigate the risk of overtrading caused by short-term market fluctuations, trading is restricted to semi-hourly intervals, specifically at HH:00 and HH:30.' Evaluate on the closed bar at the grid time.

4. TRAILING STOP, verbatim: Long TrailingStop[t][HH:MM] = max(UB[t][HH:MM], VWAP[t][HH:MM]); Short TrailingStop[t][HH:MM] = min(LB[t][HH:MM], VWAP[t][HH:MM]). 'Once a position is established, as soon as the price crosses either the current band or the VWAP, the position is closed.' VWAP is RTH-only, reset at 09:30.

5. REVERSAL: 'Positions are unwound either at market Close or if there is a crossover to the opposite boundary of the Noise Area. In the event of such a crossover, the existing position is closed, and a new one is initiated in the opposite direction.'

6. STOP TIMING: 'Stop losses can also be triggered only on semi-hourly intervals.' No resting stop order.

survivors.name: Turn of the Month in Equity Indexes (Quantpedia #41)
survivors.instrument: PRIMARY: E-mini / Micro E-mini S&P 500 futures (ES/MES). This is the only variant in the whole input set with a published, net-of-transaction-cost futures test. Also tested on DAX and Nikkei index futures by the same study — both FAILED the persistence test, so do not port the rule to FDAX or Nikkei. Quantpedia page (verified) lists Financial instruments: ETFs, Funds, Futures, CFDs, Options. SPY is the ETF proxy.
survivors.timeframe: Daily bars on the exchange session calendar. Variant A: 1 session held, 12 round trips/yr (~12 sessions exposure). Variant B: 4 sessions held, 12 round trips/yr (~48 sessions exposure).
survivors.rules:
FULLY MECHANICAL. No price data is needed to generate the signal — it is a pure exchange-calendar rule, so there is zero lookahead/repaint risk.

SETUP (both variants)
S = ordered list of regular trading sessions for the traded contract, from the exchange calendar (CME Globex equity-index calendar for ES/MES; NYSE calendar for SPY). Known years in advance.
L(m) = the last session in S whose date falls in calendar month m.

=== VARIANT A — IMPLEMENT THIS ONE (Carchano & Pardo '+1'; the only cost-tested futures version) ===
ENTRY: on session L(m), go long exactly 1 unit at that session's official close. No price condition, no filter, no confirmation, no discretion.
EXIT: on the very next session in S after L(m) (= the 1st session of month m+1), close the long at that session's official close. Unconditionally, every month, no exceptions.
Otherwise: flat. Never pyramid; exactly one unit per month.

=== VARIANT B — Quantpedia headline (-1,+3) window; the 7.2% / Sharpe 1.04 figures belong to THIS one ===
ENTRY: at the close of the session immediately preceding L(m), i.e. S[i] where S[i+1] = L(m) — the second-to-last session of month m.
EXIT: at the close of the 3rd session of month m+1.
AMBIGUITY RESOLVED: Quantpedia's 'Buy SPY ETF 1 day ... before the end of the month' is ambiguous. Resolved to 'close of the session BEFORE the last session' because the quoted statistics are the (-1,+3) return window from Table 3 Panel A1, and capturing day -1's return requires already being long at the prior close. If you instead buy at the close of L(m) you are trading a (+1,+3) window and the cited 7.2% / 1.04 Sharpe do not apply.

EXECUTION (removes the 'at the close' ambiguity)
- ES/MES: submit a market order in the window 15:59:30–16:00:00 ET; benchmark fills against the CME daily settlement price (VWAP of 15:59:30–16:00:00 ET).
- SPY: Market-On-Close order submitted before the NYSE 15:50 ET MOC cutoff.

STOP: NONE IN THE SOURCE. Every exit is time-based. The quoted return, volatility and drawdown are for a no-stop rule that always exits at the scheduled close; adding any stop changes the tested distribution and voids the cited numbers.
If your broker or prop-firm mandates a resting stop, add ONE catastrophic stop as an explicit, logged ADDITION: place at entry at entry_price*(1-k) for longs, with k = max(3 * ATR20(daily)/entry_price, the k implied by your per-trade equity cap). Never trail it, never move it. Backtest with and without and compare both equity curves before trusting either.

CONTRACT ROLL (ES/MES): roll to the next quarterly at the close of the Thursday preceding the third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec. If a roll date falls inside a held position, roll at that close (exit front, enter back, same size).

EDGE CASES
- Shortened/half sessions: trade them normally at that session's early close (13:00 ET).
- Month-end falling on an exchange closure resolves automatically because L(m) is defined off the session list, not the calendar date.
- Position sizing: 1 unit = unlevered notional equal to account equity, which is what the published statistics assume.
survivors.evidence:
VERIFIED against the live Quantpedia page. Source paper McConnell & Xu, 'Equity Returns at the Turn of the Month' (SSRN 917884), 109 years, with the authors' own out-of-sample 1987–2005 confirmation. COSTS NOT MODELLED in the 7.2% figure. The -20.79% drawdown is Quantpedia's own estimate, not the paper's.

FUTURES / COST-TESTED EVIDENCE (verified via CXO Advisory's review of Carchano & Pardo Tornero, SSRN 1958587): 188 cyclical anomalies tested on S&P 500, DAX and Nikkei index futures, Dec 1991–Apr 2008. 'Only three of 188 effects exhibit statistical significance in both of two equal sample subperiods.' The TOM '+1' effect (buying at the close on the last trading day of the month and selling at the close the next trading day) applied to S&P 500 index futures 'is the only calendar effect that persistently exhibits net profitability.' Net cumulative profit 27.5%, assuming 'round trip trading frictions of 0.05%'.

CORRECTION TO THE INPUT BRIEF: 27.5% is CUMULATIVE over the 16.4-year sample, not annual. That compounds to roughly 1.49% per annum net on unlevered notional (~0.12% net per round trip over ~197 round trips). The input list quoted 27.5% without this context, which reads far stronger than it is. At ES notional-to-margin leverage the figure scales up, but so does the risk.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE on the same Quantpedia page: Hansen & Lunde find calendar effects diminished in large caps from the late 1980s; Dzhabarov & Ziemba (JPM 2010, futures 1993–2009) still find 'there is still value in these anomalies', stronger in small caps.

The only candidate that survived an explicit stock-index-futures replication WITH transaction costs modelled, across three markets and two independent sub-periods, and 1 of only 3 survivors out of 188 tested effects. Mechanization required resolving exactly one ambiguity (the entry day), and Variant A is ambiguity-free by construction. Authorship note: Quantpedia's page cites 'Carchano & Tornero' and the input brief cites 'Carchano & Pardo' — verified as the same paper, the second author being Ángel Pardo Tornero. survivors.name: FOMC Meeting Effect / Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift
survivors.instrument: E-mini S&P 500 futures (ES) for the intraday variants — the instrument the decay literature actually measures. SPY or ES for the daily variant. Quantpedia page (verified) lists ETFs, Funds, Futures, CFDs.
survivors.timeframe: Variant A: daily bars, 1 session held per meeting, 8 events/yr (~8 sessions exposure). Variant B: intraday, ~24h held, 8 events/yr. Variant C: intraday, ~6.25h held (open to announcement).
survivors.rules:
FULLY MECHANICAL. Signal is a published calendar, not price — no lookahead risk.

SETUP
Read the Federal Reserve's published schedule of SCHEDULED FOMC meetings from federalreserve.gov (released ~1 year ahead). EXCLUDE unscheduled/emergency/intermeeting actions.
A(k) = announcement day of scheduled meeting k = the FINAL day of that meeting (day 2 of a two-day meeting; the single day of a one-day meeting).
R(k) = the scheduled statement release time for meeting k, read from the Fed calendar. DO NOT HARDCODE: it is 14:00 ET currently, was 14:15 ET before 2013.

=== VARIANT A — daily; the version the quoted 6.19% belongs to ===
ENTRY: long 1 unit at the close of the session immediately preceding A(k).
EXIT: close the long at the close of A(k). Unconditionally. Otherwise flat.
AMBIGUITY RESOLVED: Quantpedia's 'closing position on close after the meeting' is ambiguous between the announcement-day close and the following day's close. Resolved to the ANNOUNCEMENT-DAY close because (i) the 6.19% is built from a single average daily return of 0.2734% times 8 meetings plus 4% on cash, and (ii) Quantpedia's own text says exposure is '8 days during the average year' — a two-session hold would be 16 days.

=== VARIANT B — Lucca & Moench 24h window; the version with the stated Sharpe of 1.14 ===
ENTRY: long 1 unit at 14:00:00 ET on the session immediately preceding A(k).
EXIT: flat at exactly R(k) minus 15 minutes on day A(k) — 13:45:00 ET under the current 14:00 ET release; 14:00:00 ET under the pre-2013 14:15 ET release. Otherwise flat.

=== VARIANT C — Kurov/Wolfe/Gilbert measurement window; use this to re-measure current decay before risking capital ===
ENTRY: long 1 unit at 09:30:00 ET on the session immediately preceding A(k). EXIT: flat at R(k) minus 15 minutes on A(k). Instrument: ES nearby contract.

EXECUTION
- Daily closes: ES market order 15:59:30–16:00:00 ET benchmarked to CME daily settlement; SPY MOC before the 15:50 ET cutoff.
- Intraday timestamps: market order at the stated wall-clock second, ET, using exchange timestamps (not local machine time). Handle DST via the America/New_York tz database, never a fixed UTC offset.

STOP: NONE IN THE SOURCE. All exits are time-based; Variants B and C are inherently time-stopped within the session. If a resting stop is mandated, use the same single catastrophic non-trailing stop construction described in the Turn-of-Month entry, logged as an addition, and compare with/without curves.

CONTRACT ROLL (ES): roll to the next quarterly at the close of the Thursday preceding the third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec.

EDGE CASES
- If the session preceding A(k) is a shortened session ending 13:00 ET, Variant B's 14:00 ET entry does not exist: use that session's close instead and flag the event in the log.
- Announcement days are not half days in practice; guard anyway.
- If a scheduled meeting is extended or the release time moved, take A(k) and R(k) from the updated Fed calendar as of the morning of A(k).
survivors.evidence:
VERIFIED against the live Quantpedia page: backtest period 1980–2000; Indicative Performance 6.19% p.a. (from 'average daily return 0.2734%' plus 4% on cash); Estimated Volatility 'not stated'; Max Drawdown -8.74% (Quantpedia notes the source does not state it); no Sharpe on the card; Confidence 'Strong'; instruments ETFs/Funds/Futures/CFDs. Costs NOT modelled. Source: Tori, reporting FOMC dates were 4.42% of trading days but over 13% of cumulative returns.

VERIFIED Lucca & Moench (NY Fed Staff Report 512 / SSRN 1923197): more than 80% of the US equity premium since 1994 was earned in the 24 hours before scheduled announcements; buying the S&P 500 at 2pm the day before and selling fifteen minutes before the announcement, holding cash otherwise, produced an annualized Sharpe of 1.14.

VERIFIED DECAY (Kurov, Wolfe & Gilbert, Finance Research Letters vol. 40, 2021), measured on E-mini S&P 500 nearby futures from the stock market open on the day before the announcement to 15 minutes before it:
  Sep 1994 – Mar 2011: 49.2 bp per meeting (in-sample)
  Apr 2011 – Dec 2015: 44.5 bp
  Jan 2016 – Dec 2019: 9.2 bp
  Apr 2011 – Dec 2019 combined: 4.7 bp
Authors attribute the collapse to reduced uncertainty (lower VIX, post-ZLB-liftoff in Dec 2015), not to arbitrage.

CORRECTIONS TO THE INPUT BRIEF: (1) the brief's '-5.1 bp for announcements without press conferences' is moot going forward — since January 2019 every scheduled FOMC meeting has a press conference, so that subsample is no longer a live category; the forward-looking estimate is 9.2 bp. (2) Kurov's window (open-to-announcement) is NOT Lucca & Moench's window (2pm-to-2pm); the brief conflates them. They are different trades and only Variant C matches the decay figures above.
survivors.why_credible: Independently documented by the New York Fed, measured on intraday ES futures rather than spot, with an explicit quantified post-publication decay study. Mechanizes cleanly: the calendar is public and published a year ahead, and entry and exit are wall-clock timestamps. Credible as a live edge only at the decayed magnitude — 9.2 bp per meeting times 8 meetings is roughly 0.7%/yr gross on unlevered notional before slippage, versus 3.9%/yr at the original 49.2 bp. Kurov's VIX-based explanation implies it could partially return in a high-volatility regime, which makes a VIX-conditional version a legitimate research direction but NOT a tested rule — do not add such a filter and then claim this paper's evidence for it.

survivors.name: Option-Expiration Week Effect (Stivers & Sun)
survivors.instrument: S&P 100 constituents (the tested universe). Quantpedia page (verified) lists ETFs, Futures, CFDs, Stocks and says the stocks 'could be easily tracked via ETF or index fund'. OEF (iShares S&P 100 ETF) is the faithful single-ticker proxy. ES futures are an UNTESTED proxy — the documented effect is specific to option-active large caps, not to the S&P 500 index or its futures.
survivors.timeframe: Weekly. 5 sessions held per event (Friday close to Friday close), 12 events/yr, 12 round trips/yr.
survivors.rules:
MECHANICAL. Signal is a pure calendar rule.

SETUP
S = ordered list of regular trading sessions from the exchange calendar.
For each calendar month m: X(m) = the standard monthly equity-option expiration date = the third Friday of month m. IF that Friday is an exchange holiday (e.g. Good Friday in some Aprils), X(m) moves to the immediately preceding session (Thursday).
OE_WEEK(m) = the sessions from the Monday of X(m)'s week through X(m) inclusive.

ENTRY: long 1 unit at the close of the last session in S strictly before the Monday of OE_WEEK(m) — normally the preceding Friday; the preceding Thursday if that Friday is a holiday.
EXIT: close the long at the close of X(m). Unconditionally. Otherwise flat. Exactly one unit per month.
This reproduces the Friday-close-to-Friday-close weekly return the source measures.

UNIVERSE (choose ONE at build time and never switch at runtime):
(a) FAITHFUL: equal-weighted basket of the current S&P 100 constituents, rebalanced to equal weight at each entry. This is what was tested.
(b) PRACTICAL PROXY: OEF ETF, 1 unit. Cap-weighted rather than the paper's construction — a documented deviation.
(c) FUTURES PROXY: ES/MES. NOT TESTED by the source. The effect is attributed to delta-hedge unwind in option-active single names; assuming it transfers to the index future is an assumption, not a result. If you use (c) you are running a new experiment and none of the cited statistics apply to it.

EXECUTION: equities/ETF MOC before the NYSE 15:50 ET cutoff; ES/MES market order 15:59:30–16:00:00 ET benchmarked to CME daily settlement.

STOP: NONE IN THE SOURCE. Time-based exit only. Same single catastrophic non-trailing stop construction if one is mandated, logged as an addition. With universe (a) a per-name stop would fragment the basket — apply any mandated stop at PORTFOLIO level, not per constituent.

EDGE CASES
- Half sessions inside OE week: trade normally; exit at the 13:00 ET early close if X(m) itself is short.
- Do NOT trade the fourth-Friday week: the source explicitly reports that 'a month's fourth-Friday weekly returns underperform modestly.'
- Basket construction for (a): use the constituent list as of the entry date; do not backfill index membership (survivorship bias).
survivors.evidence:
VERIFIED against the live Quantpedia page: backtest period 1988–2010 (22 years); Indicative Performance 9.3% p.a. (weekly return 0.528% x 12 weeks from table 3, plus ~3/4 x 4% on cash); Estimated Volatility 8.7%; Max Drawdown -15.14% (Quantpedia's estimate — the source does not state it); Sharpe 0.61; Confidence 'Strong'; instruments ETFs/Futures/CFDs/Stocks. Costs NOT modelled. The page defines the window as the week before options expiration, the Friday before each third Saturday — i.e. the week ending on the third Friday, which is what the rule above implements.

Mechanism stated by the source: '(1) delta-hedge rebalancing by option market makers, with a reduction in short-stock hedge positions over the OE week, and (2) declining risk perceptions over the OE week, as measured by option-derived implied volatilities.'

DECAY: not directly tested. Indirect and partly contradictory follow-ups cited on the same page: Cao, Chordia & Zhan (SSRN 3659479) find third-Friday selling pressure from expiration-related stock delivery; Mohamed & Hussein (SSRN 5101935) test options-expiration dates alongside other calendar effects across the S&P 500/400/600 and Russell 1000 Growth/Value using ARMA(1,1)+EGARCH(1,1) and rank the Halloween effect, not options expiration, as the most significant anomaly observed.
survivors.why_credible: Unusually concrete mechanism for a calendar effect — market-maker delta-hedge unwind is a real, dated flow rather than a mood story — and the source controls it against three separate benchmarks (less option-active stocks, the same stocks' other weeks, and asset-pricing alphas). Mechanizes cleanly. Main caveats: Sharpe only 0.61; the drawdown is Quantpedia's estimate rather than the paper's; the effect is documented on S&P 100 single names, so the index-futures implementation this project would actually want is an untested extrapolation; and the most recent multi-index study on the page ranks it below the Halloween effect.

survivors.name: Payday Anomaly (Ma & Pratt)

survivors.timeframe: Daily bars. 1 session held per event. 12 events/yr under the default convention below, or roughly 7/yr under the literal convention — this materially changes the expected return.
survivors.rules:
MECHANICAL, but ONLY after pinning a convention the source never states. Read the resolution below before implementing — it is worth roughly 40% of the headline return.

EXIT: close the long at the close of E(m). Unconditionally. Otherwise flat. Exactly one unit per month.

VERIFIED against the live Quantpedia page: the rule is 'holding the S&P500 index on the 16th day of the month', confirmed as the CALENDAR day rather than the 16th trading day; backtest period 1980–2010 (30 years); Indicative Performance 2.57% p.a. from an annualized mean return of 0.214% in table 4 panel B; Estimated Volatility 4.31% (computed by Quantpedia from the t-stat of 3.07); Max Drawdown -12.06% (Quantpedia notes the source does not state it); Sharpe 0.6; Confidence 'Strong'; Notes to Confidence: none present. survivors.name: Pre-Holiday Effect
survivors.instrument: US equity market index. Quantpedia page (verified) lists ETFs, Funds, Futures, CFDs. Source paper tested indices from Denmark, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Italy, Japan, Norway, Sweden, the UK and the US.
survivors.timeframe: Daily bars. 1 session held per event. 9 events/yr under a modern US exchange calendar — NOT the 10 the source assumed. See rules.
survivors.rules:
MECHANICAL, but only after resolving three calendar problems the source leaves open. All three are resolved below with a stated default.

SETUP
S = ordered list of regular trading sessions from the exchange calendar of the traded instrument.
H = the source's holiday list, verified verbatim on the page: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, President's Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Election Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day.
For each closure in H that actually closes the exchange in year y, define P = the last session in S strictly before that closure (the 'pre-holiday session').

ENTRY: long 1 unit at the close of the session immediately preceding P.
EXIT: close the long at the close of P. Unconditionally. Otherwise flat. Exactly one unit per event; never pyramid if two events fall adjacent.

THREE CALENDAR RESOLUTIONS — each is a decision the source does not make. Implement the DEFAULT; treat the alternative as a separately labelled variant, never a runtime choice:
1. ELECTION DAY — DEFAULT: EXCLUDE. The NYSE stopped closing for Election Day after 1984, so no pre-holiday session exists for it under the definition above. This drops the count from 10 events/yr to 9, which means Quantpedia's 6.39% (built as 0.239% x 10 holidays + 4% cash) overstates a modern implementation by roughly a tenth of the equity leg. Alternative variant: define Election Day as the first Tuesday after the first Monday of November and treat the preceding session as an event despite there being no closure — untested; do not mix it with the headline statistics.
2. JUNETEENTH — DEFAULT: EXCLUDE. It became an NYSE/CME closure only in 2022, is not in the source's list, and is entirely out of sample. Test as a separate variant if at all.
3. HALF SESSIONS — the pre-holiday session is frequently a shortened session (3 July, Christmas Eve). DEFAULT: trade them normally and exit at that session's EARLY CLOSE, 13:00 ET. survivors.rules:
VERIFIED AGAINST SOURCE: src/noise_area.py, src/backtest.py, src/sizing.py (all three read in full).

INDICATORS, per session D and minute-of-day t (bar HH:MM covers [HH:MM, HH:MM+1)):
- O_D = open of the day's first RTH bar; C_prev = close of the previous session's last RTH bar.
- move(d,t) = abs(close(d,t)/O_d - 1).
- sigma(D,t) = mean of move(d,t) over the previous 14 SESSIONS at that same minute-of-day, current day EXCLUDED (pivot days x minute-of-day, rolling(14, min_periods=7).mean().shift(1) on the day axis). If NaN, no action at that check.
- Upper(D,t) = max(O_D, C_prev) * (1 + sigma(D,t)); Lower(D,t) = min(O_D, C_prev) * (1 - sigma(D,t)).
- VWAP(D,t) = cumsum from 09:30 of ((H+L+C)/3 * volume) / cumsum of volume.
- sigma_daily(D) = std (ddof=1) of the last 14 session-close-to-session-close returns, shifted 1 day (no look-ahead). If NaN, no NEW position may be opened.

CHECK GRID: every 30 minutes from 10:00 while <= 15:45, i.e. 10:00...15:30. At each check take the LAST bar at or before the check time (sparse feeds fall back to the last traded price); px = that bar's close; upper/lower/vwap from that same bar.
- long_sig = px > upper; short_sig = px < lower.
- FLAT: long_sig -> open long at px; else short_sig -> open short at px.
- LONG: if short_sig -> close at px AND immediately open a short at px (flip, both legs charged). Else compute trail = lower ('base' variant) | max(vwap, upper) ('final' variant) | vwap ('vwap' variant); if px < trail -> close at px.
- SHORT: if long_sig -> close and flip to long at px. Else trail = upper ('base') | min(vwap, lower) ('final') | vwap ('vwap'); if px > trail -> close at px.
- END OF SESSION: if still positioned, close at the close of the day's last RTH bar (15:59). Never overnight.
There is no hard stop-loss: the trailing band/VWAP test at the 30-minute checks IS the stop, so worst-case intraday adverse excursion between checks is uncapped.

SIZING at every open: exposure = min(equity * 0.02 / sigma_daily(D), 4.0 * equity); units = floor(exposure / (fill_price * multiplier)); if units <= 0, no position. multiplier = 1 (SPY shares), 50 (ES), 5 (MES). Equity compounds.

FILLS/COSTS, charged per leg: fill = px + slip when buying, px - slip when selling, slip = slippage_per_unit / multiplier. ES/MES: commission $0.85 + fees $1.40 per contract PER LEG, slippage 0.25 tick = $3.125 per contract per leg (so ~$9.25/contract round trip, ~0.4 bps). SPY: $0.0035/share with a $0.35 per-order minimum, baseline slippage 0.

FROZEN PARAMETERS (spec, do not optimise): lookback 14 days, check interval 30 min, vol target 2%/day, max leverage 4x, vol lookback 14 days.

DISCREPANCY TO FLAG: the paper defines the 'final' long trailing stop as max(VWAP, LOWER band); this repo implements max(VWAP, UPPER band) — i.e. a long is cut the moment price falls back INSIDE the noise area. The repo's docstring states this deliberately ('re-entry into the Noise Area, or a cross of the session VWAP'). Implement whichever you mean, but know they are different strategies and the repo's own numbers are for its version.

survivors.timeframe: 5-minute bars, RTH, US/Eastern. 1 Jan 2016 – 17 Feb 2023 (both dates confirmed in the paper's Table 1). Interactive Brokers data, MATLAB R2022.
survivors.rules:
MECHANICAL SPEC. Bars: bar1 = 09:30:00–09:35:00, bar2 = 09:35:00–09:40:00.
1. DIRECTION — evaluated once, at the close of bar1 (09:35:00): if Close1 > Open1 -> LONG; if Close1 < Open1 -> SHORT; if Close1 == Open1 -> NO TRADE.
2. ENTRY — market order filled at Open2 (the 09:35:00 print). Set P = Open2.
3. RISK UNIT — LONG: StopPrice = Low1. SHORT: StopPrice = High1. $R = abs(P - StopPrice). If $R == 0, skip the day (guards divide-by-zero).
4. SIZE — Shares = floor( min( A*0.01/$R , 4*A/P ) ), where A = account equity at 09:30 that day. If Shares < 1, skip.
5. TARGET — LONG: P + 10*$R. SHORT: P - 10*$R.
6. RESTING ORDERS — stop at StopPrice and limit at target, both live 09:35:00 to 16:00:00.
7. EXIT — the first of: (a) stop touched, (b) target touched, (c) 16:00:00 market-on-close.
8. COSTS — $0.0005/share on entry and again on exit. Slippage = 0 (the paper's explicit assumption, Table 1: 'We assumed no slippage in fills.').
9. Starting capital $25,000. One position per day, no re-entry, no overnight hold.

TWO DISCRETION POINTS THE PAPER LEAVES OPEN — you must pin them:
(a) DOJI. The 2023 paper writes 'a doji (open ~ close)' — the tilde is undefined. The same authors' 2024 successor paper writes 'a doji (open = close)'. RESOLUTION: use exact equality Close1 == Open1. On real QQQ 5-min data this fires on well under 1% of days, so the choice is low-impact, but it must be fixed in code.
(b) INTRABAR STOP-vs-TARGET. If one 5-min bar's range contains both the stop and the 10R target, the paper does not say which filled first. RESOLUTION: resolve on 1-minute bars; if only 5-min bars are available, assume the STOP fills first (conservative, and near-certainly correct given the target sits 10x further away).

survivors.name: Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon — 'Beat the Market' intraday momentum (Noise Area), SPY plus a 12-equity-index futures extension [VERIFIED, FULLY MECHANICAL — but NOT an ORB, and the incoming summary mislabelled the results rows]
survivors.instrument: Primary: SPY. Extension (FAQ Q13): 33 global futures markets — 21 commodities and 12 equity indices — of which four are named: Nasdaq, S&P 500, Russell, S&P 400 MidCap. NOTE: this is a volatility-scaled intraday momentum band breach, NOT an opening range breakout.
survivors.timeframe: SPY: 2007 to early 2024 (17 years). Futures extension: January 2007 – September 2024. Entries, stops and reversals are evaluated ONLY on semi-hourly marks (HH:00 and HH:30).
survivors.rules:
MECHANICAL SPEC — every formula below verified verbatim from the paper.
1. NOISE AREA, step 1 — for each prior day t-i (i = 1..14) and each minute HH:MM of the session: move(t-i, HH:MM) = | Close(t-i, HH:MM) / Open(t-i, 09:30) - 1 |.
2. Step 2 — sigma(t, HH:MM) = (1/14) * sum over i=1..14 of move(t-i, HH:MM). Note this is a mean of ABSOLUTE moves, not a standard deviation, and it is TIME-OF-DAY SPECIFIC: the band at 10:00 is built only from prior days' 09:30-to-10:00 moves.
3. Step 3, WITH the overnight-gap adjustment (use this version, not the unadjusted one):
   UpperBound(t, HH:MM) = max( Open(t,09:30), Close(t-1,16:00) ) * (1 + m * sigma(t,HH:MM))
   LowerBound(t, HH:MM) = min( Open(t,09:30), Close(t-1,16:00) ) * (1 - m * sigma(t,HH:MM))
   where m is the volatility multiplier, set to 1 in the paper. Anchoring to max/min against the previous close is what absorbs overnight gaps.
4. DECISION POINTS — evaluate ONLY at HH:00 and HH:30. Everything below happens at those marks and nowhere else, including stops. This is the paper's explicit anti-overtrading device.
5. ENTRY — if flat and Price > UpperBound -> go LONG. If flat and Price < LowerBound -> go SHORT.
6. TRAILING STOP, verbatim formulas:
   Long TrailingStop(t,HH:MM)  = max( UpperBound(t,HH:MM), VWAP(t,HH:MM) )
   Short TrailingStop(t,HH:MM) = min( LowerBound(t,HH:MM), VWAP(t,HH:MM) )
   'Once a position is established, as soon as the price crosses either the current band or the VWAP, the position is closed.' VWAP is computed from RTH data only, anchored at 09:30 of day t.
7. REVERSAL — on a crossover to the OPPOSITE boundary, close and immediately open the opposite position.
8. FORCED FLAT at 16:00. No overnight exposure.
9. SIZING (the volatility-targeted version that produces the headline number):
   Shares(t) = AUM(t-1) * min( 4, 0.02 / sigma_SPY(t) ) / Open(t, 09:30)
   where sigma_SPY(t) is the SAMPLE standard deviation of the last 14 daily returns using denominator 13 (i.e. n-1), and 0.02 is the 2% daily volatility target. The min(4, ...) is the 4x leverage cap.
10. COSTS — commission $0.0035/share (IB entry-level) plus slippage $0.001/share.

survivors.rules:
MECHANICAL as a universe specification. Again an acceptance-test spec, not one strategy.

1. BUILD 39,832 rules and strategies, broken down exactly as published: 18,326 simple trading rules + 18,326 contrarian rules (each simple rule with its signal inverted) + 3,180 investor's strategies.
2. THE 12 SIMPLE CLASSES: filter rules; moving averages; support and resistance; channel breakouts; on-balance volume; momentum in price; momentum in volume; head-and-shoulders; triangle; rectangle; double tops and bottoms; broadening tops and bottoms.
3. THE 3 INVESTOR'S-STRATEGY TYPES, which is Hsu-Kuan's addition and matters most to a bot builder: LEARNING strategies (at each date, select the rule with the best performance so far and follow it); VOTE strategies (take the majority signal across a rule class); POSITION-CHANGEABLE strategies. These are meta-strategies over the rule set — exactly what an adaptive or auto-optimising bot is, whether or not it is described that way.
4. EVALUATE on daily closing returns with White's Reality Check over the full universe, with transaction costs included, then confirm on the untouched 2001 and 2002 windows.
5. ACCEPT only if the universe-adjusted p-value is significant AND the out-of-sample windows hold.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: if your bot re-selects its best-performing configuration over time, you have built a learning strategy, and you must correct for the full universe it selects from — not just the configuration currently running.
survivors.evidence: Both claims verified verbatim from the paper PDF. On STW, verbatim: "Sullivan, Timmermann, and White (1999), henceforth STW, and White (2000) applied this test and found that there exists no profitable simple trading rule for Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) index, S&P 500 index, and S&P 500 futures." Hsu & Kuan's own finding, verbatim from their abstract: "It is found that profitable simple rules and investor's strategies do exist with statistical significance for NASDAQ Composite and Russell 2000 but not for DJIA and S&P 500. Moreover, the best rules for NASDAQ Composite and Russell 2000 outperform the buy-and-hold strategy in most in- and out-of-sample periods, even when transaction costs are taken into account." The structure of the result is the point: expanding the universe roughly five-fold from 7,846 to 39,832 and adding adaptive meta-strategies STILL found nothing on the mature large-cap indices. Only the younger NASDAQ Composite and Russell 2000 survive, and the authors attribute that explicitly to market maturity. Rule counts verified from the paper's own table: simple 18,326, contrarian 18,326, investor's strategies 3,180, total 39,832 (35,776 for Russell 2000 due to data availability).
survivors.why_credible: VERIFIED: I downloaded and text-extracted the PDF and confirmed the abstract, the STW citation sentence, the rule-count table and the exact in/out-of-sample observation counts. critique:
## 1. Which survivor plausibly beats 1.16R/month at <10R DD?

**None.** State the incumbent's real figure first, because it's the bar everything else fails:

13.9R/yr against 10.3R MaxDD = **MAR 1.35**; per-trade SD = 0.052·√349 = 0.97R, so monthly Sharpe = 1.16/(0.97·√7.9) = 0.42, **annualised Sharpe ≈ 1.47**. That is better than every honest out-of-sample number in the survivor set.

| Candidate | Best honest OOS | Return/MaxDD per yr |
|---|---|---|
| Incumbent NQ retest | +0.146R, SR 1.47 | **1.35** |
| Quantitativo NQ (90d/3%/8x) | 24.3% / MDD 24%, **no OOS at all** | 1.01 |
| Zarattini SPY headline (final+vol target) | 19.6% / MDD 25% | 0.78 |
| Brusco ES base (real 2024-26 OOS) | 7.8% / MDD 16.3% | 0.48 |
| Brusco ES final (real OOS) | −2.1% / MDD 22.7% | negative |
| Turn-of-Month ES net | ~1.5%/yr | ~0.1 |
| FOMC (decayed, 9.2bp×8) | ~0.7%/yr | ~0.1 |
| Payday / OpEx / Pre-holiday | 0.4–2.6%/yr gross, unreplicated or futures-failed | <0.3 |

The closest thing to a real candidate is the **Noise Area BASE variant on NQ** (not the headline variant), and it is worth stating mechanically because it is the answer to Q4:

- σ(t,HH:MM) = mean over the prior 90 sessions of |Close(d,HH:MM)/Open(d,09:30) − 1|
- UB = max(Open₀₉:₃₀, PrevClose₁₆:₀₀)·(1+σ); LB = min(…)·(1−σ)
- Decisions only at HH:00/HH:30, 10:00–15:30 ET. Flat: P>UB → long, P<LB → short.
- **Base exit: only on a cross of the opposite band, which also reverses.** No VWAP trail.
- Hard flat at 16:00. Size = floor(AUM·min(4, 0.02/σ_daily)/(Open·20)).

**Cost/R is not the problem here, and that matters.** With the opposite-band stop, R = UB−LB ≈ 2σ·price ≈ 260 NQ points at midday. Round trip at futures tick = 0.44 pts → **cost/R = 0.17%**; on a prop CFD at 1.34 spread + 1.0 slippage = 2.34 pts → **0.9%**. Both sit *below* NQ's already-survivable 1.4%, i.e. an order of magnitude under the ~4% cliff your own table locates between DAX (+0.009R) and ES (−0.087R). Frequency is 0.61 trades/day (Brusco: 326 trades / 530 ES days) ≈ 13/month, 1.6× the incumbent.

But its measured MAR is 0.48 — 2.8× worse than what you already hold. **It clears the cost test and fails the return/drawdown test.** So: no survivor qualifies.

## 2. Search modality not run

**The holding-horizon dimension.** Every model you tested — ORB, retest, sweep, and every literature candidate you evaluated — is intraday-flat-by-close. You searched signals × instruments × parameters × sessions, but never horizon.

This matters because cost/R = cost / stop-distance, cost per round trip is fixed by the venue, and you already established cost/R is *the* binding constraint. Stop distance grows roughly with √(holding time); cost does not grow at all. Concretely, on the same seven markets:

| Market | cost/R at 5-min OR | cost/R at 2×ATR(14 daily) |
|---|---|---|
| NQ | 1.4% | ~0.05% |
| DAX | 4.5% | ~0.4% |
| ES | 6.1% | ~0.5% |
| FTSE | 10.0% | ~1.0% |
| EuroStoxx | 23.8% | ~2.4% |

**A multi-day horizon makes all seven of your dead markets cost-survivable**, including EuroStoxx, which is currently 17× over the cliff. That is a 10–30× improvement on the exact variable you identified as binding, and it is the only lever available: you already used futures-tick costs, so the cost numerator cannot be reduced further.

What it would likely find: not a new signal, but the *same* structural signals working where they currently can't. The honest prediction is time-series momentum / multi-day breakout / carry at Sharpe 0.7–1.1 per market with correlation 0.5–0.8 across equity indices, ~0.2 once you add FX, rates and commodities.

A note on the instrument-swap alternative, which looks attractive and isn't: NQ's 1.4% is exceptional because of a very high index level against a 0.25-point tick and a deep book. Run the arithmetic on the obvious substitutes — EURUSD raw (~0.7 pip round-trip commission-equivalent against a 10–15 pip 5-min OR ≈ 5%), XAUUSD (~$0.25 against a $4 OR ≈ 6%) — and they land in ES/YM territory, not NQ territory. The only intraday instruments in NQ's cost/R class are NQ, MNQ, and possibly BTC/ETH perpetuals on a low-fee venue (0.5bp against a ~0.4% OR ≈ 1.2%). **Instrument substitution buys you nothing intraday; horizon extension buys you 10–30×.**

## 3. A class with a fundamentally different profile

Yes, and it is not higher frequency — it is **breadth at a longer horizon**.

Higher frequency is unavailable: the only way to trade more often without spread scaling is to *earn* the spread rather than pay it, which requires queue priority you cannot get on a prop CFD account with a deviation cap.

The class that fits the cost structure is **multi-day diversified time-series momentum / breakout across 15–25 futures or CFD markets** (equity indices, FX majors, rates, energy, metals), 5–40 day holds, stop at 2–3×ATR(14 daily), 0.25% risk per market, monthly or signal-driven rebalance. Cost/R 0.05–0.5%, i.e. costs become a rounding error rather than the deciding term. Century-scale out-of-sample evidence (Moskowitz–Ooi–Pedersen; Hurst–Ooi–Pedersen), which is a different evidential class from anything in your survivor file.

**The honest catch, and it is the crux of Q5:** portfolio Sharpe scales as √N in *independent* bets, so 20 markets at Sharpe 0.8 and correlation 0.2 gives portfolio Sharpe ~1.6 — comparable to what you already have. What it buys is not a bigger edge but *more bets per unit calendar time*, which is exactly what a fixed-deadline ruin race needs. What it costs is drawdown duration: TSMOM drawdowns run 12–24 months, which is compatible with a 10% static cap only if there is no time limit, and incompatible with any fast-pass requirement.

Also worth flagging: **your portfolio test does not refute diversification.** You added legs with measured edges of +0.013R and −0.025R — i.e. nothing — so DD rose 10.3R→35.0R and return/DD fell 0.113→0.041 exactly as arithmetic predicts. That result refutes diversifying *into zero*, not diversification. The correct test is N legs each independently clearing +0.10R, which you have never had more than one of.

## 4. Killed for a weak reason

**The Quantitativo Noise Area ES/NQ port (and by extension the Zarattini base variant).**

It was killed on evidence-provenance and specifiability. Neither reason survives contact with your own binding constraint:

- **The cost reviewer explicitly declined to refute it**: "CANNOT REFUTE ON COSTS — the strategy clears the 0.15R kill line by roughly an order of magnitude." That is the only lens that has predicted your results correctly.
- **The specifiability kill is closable.** The objection was that the newsletter defers its rules to the paper. The paper is in your survivor set fully specified (formulas verbatim), and Brusco's repo is an executable reference implementation with 48 unit tests. The four "free parameters" (decision grid, which stop, gap adjustment, σ estimator) are all pinned by the paper's own text.
- **The version that was actually measured is the wrong version.** The SPY Noise Area was measured on your data at +0.067R/trade, t=0.38, decaying monotonically — but that was the **final** variant (max(band, VWAP) trail). Brusco's cross-instrument work reports that in the 2024–26 regime *the paper's hierarchy inverts*: base beats final on both SPY and ES (ES base SR 0.52 vs final −0.07). Nobody has measured the base variant on your NDXUSD M1 data.
- It is the only candidate that simultaneously has cost/R ≈ 0.2–0.9% on NQ, 1.6× your current trade frequency, a public reference implementation, and no measurement on your own data in its currently-best-performing form.

Expected outcome if you run it: MAR ~0.5, i.e. it will probably not beat the incumbent. But it is one afternoon of work on data you already hold, it tests the *base* variant specifically, and it is the only remaining intraday candidate whose failure mode would be informative rather than predicted.

Second-weakest kill, for the record: **the portfolio-combination result** (see Q3) — refuted zero-edge legs, not the lever.

## 5. The case that no such edge exists, and what follows

**The argument, in four steps:**

1. **Pass probability is a function of Sharpe alone; leverage cancels.** A prop challenge sets the target (+10%) and the ruin barrier (−10%) in the same units. Scaling risk scales both. So P(pass) depends only on the strategy's Sharpe over the challenge horizon and the number of independent bets inside it — which is precisely why your Monte Carlo saturates at 57% with 43% blow-ups *regardless of leverage*. That is not an implementation failure; it is the correct answer to the question you asked. To reach 80%+ in a one-month window you need annualised Sharpe ≈ 3.

2. **No replicated intraday index strategy has Sharpe 3 net of costs.** The best honest OOS numbers in your entire survivor file are 1.24–1.34 (Zarattini, static size) and 1.11 (Brusco replication) — and both went to ~0 or negative in 2025–26 on two instruments and two independent data vendors at 0.97 daily correlation. Your own measured 1.47 is *the best number in the file*.

3. **Four independent multiple-testing-corrected sweeps return nulls on exactly this market.** Sullivan–Timmermann–White: 7,846 rules, nothing on DJIA/S&P/S&P futures. Hsu–Kuan: 39,832 rules including adaptive meta-strategies, nothing on mature large caps (only NASDAQ Composite and Russell 2000 survive, attributed to market immaturity). Carchano–Pardo: 188 cyclical effects on ES/DAX/Nikkei futures, 1 survivor at ~1.5%/yr net. Mesfin: 14 intraday families on MNQ 2021–25, none above friction. Your own ORB holdout, where the best-fitted filters inverted to worst, is a fifth instance of the same result.

4. **Every candidate with a genuine post-publication OOS test decayed.** Gao et al. → Rosa (JFM 2022, "predictability disappears"), Baltussen (ES R²_OOS −1.68), QuantConnect (SR −0.628). Bondarenko–Muravyev → NY Fed, "The Disappearing Overnight Drift," 2026. Zarattini → Brusco, negative on both instruments since 2025. This is the McLean–Pontiff base rate operating on the most competed intraday market in the world.

**What follows: neither of your two options as stated.**

Do not scale ambition down to 0.58%/month, and do not change instrument class. **Change the constraint, not the strategy.** MAR 1.35 at Sharpe 1.47 is a top-decile result — most professional CTAs run MAR 0.3–0.7. It fails only against a one-month 1:1 ruin race, which is a format problem, not an edge problem. Specifically:

- **Deploy the NQ retest against a mandate it can win**: own capital, or a firm with a static (not trailing) drawdown and no time limit. At Sharpe 1.47 a 10% target with a 10% barrier and unlimited time is a waiting problem with high pass probability, not a coin flip. Do not attempt the one-month format — your own Monte Carlo says 0%, and that number is structural.
- **Spend the next unit of effort on horizon, not on more intraday signals.** It is the only lever that moves cost/R by 10–30×, it resurrects all five markets you killed on cost, and it is the one dimension of the search space you have never touched. Concretely: re-run your existing model family on daily bars with 2–3×ATR stops across the seven indices you already have data for, then extend the universe to FX/rates/commodities for uncorrelated breadth.
- **Run the Noise Area base variant on NQ once** (Q4), because it is cheap and it is the only intraday candidate not yet falsified in the form that currently works.
- **Only add portfolio legs that independently clear +0.10R.** Your 10.3R→35.0R result is the correct penalty for doing otherwise, and it will recur.

The realistic ceiling under any 10% drawdown cap is roughly 8–13%/yr regardless of strategy, because MAR tops out near 1.4 across everything documented. Any plan that requires 10% in a month is requiring a MAR the literature does not contain.
